        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/msym
        

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the primary focus of the Mahila Samridhi Yojana in terms of community development?
The scheme primarily focuses on enhancing the socio-economic standing of the Charmakar community by promoting self-reliance through financial assistance.
Is there any financial cap on the subsidies or benefits provided under the scheme?
Yes, loans are capped between ₹25,000 and ₹50,000 per beneficiary, with a low-interest rate of 4% per annum.
Can male members of the Charmakar community apply under this scheme?
No, the Mahila Samridhi Yojana is specifically designed to provide financial assistance to female members of the Charmakar community.
How does the Mahila Samridhi Yojana contribute to the socio-economic development of its beneficiaries?
By offering financial assistance at a low-interest rate and prioritising socially disadvantaged categories such as widows and divorcees, the scheme enables economic independence and enhances the quality of life for beneficiaries.
Is there any training or skill development assistance provided under the Mahila Samridhi Yojana?
No specific training is mentioned in the scheme guidelines, but applicants are expected to have prior knowledge of the business they wish to pursue.
What role does the Leather Industries Development Corporation of Maharashtra (LIDCOM) play in this scheme?
LIDCOM oversees the distribution of application forms, processing of applications, and facilitation of financial assistance for eligible beneficiaries.
Does the Mahila Samridhi Yojana assist in the production and sale of goods?
Yes, the scheme supports the production of footwear and leather articles, which are either supplied to government departments or sold in the open market.
Where can eligible applicants obtain the application form for the Mahila Samridhi Yojana?
The application form is available at the District Office of the Leather Industries Development Corporation of Maharashtra (LIDCOM).
Are there any special priorities for certain categories of beneficiaries under the Mahila Samridhi Yojana?
Yes, special priority is given to widows and divorcees within the Charmakar community when providing financial assistance.
What kind of financial assistance is provided to beneficiaries under the Mahila Samridhi Yojana?
Loans ranging from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000 are provided to eligible beneficiaries at an interest rate of 4% per annum.
Is there a specific age range for applicants to be eligible for the scheme?
Yes, applicants must be between 18 and 50 years of age to apply for benefits under the Mahila Samridhi Yojana.
Are there any specific business requirements for applicants under this scheme?
Yes, applicants must possess adequate knowledge about the business for which they are seeking financial assistance under the scheme.
What proof of eligibility needs to be submitted while applying for the Mahila Samridhi Yojana?
Applicants need to submit income and caste certificates issued by an authorised government officer and provide proof of permanent residency in Maharashtra.
What are the income limits for applicants to qualify for the Mahila Samridhi Yojana in rural and urban areas?
To qualify for the scheme, applicants' annual income must be below ₹98,000 in rural areas and below ₹1,20,000 in urban areas.

Details
The scheme "Mahila Samridhi Yojana under NSKFDC" is implemented by the Haryana Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (HSFDC) in collaboration with the National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation (NSKFDC). The HSFDC is a Company registered under the Companies Act, 1956 on 02.01.1971. This scheme offers loans up to ₹1,00,000/- to women Safai Karamcharis or their dependents for economic development through self-employment initiatives, such as establishing cloth shops, dairies, tea shops, bangle shops, beauty parlours, papad making, basketry, tailoring shops, etc. The Corporation contributes margin money at 10% of the project cost.

Subsidy:
The corporation provides a subsidy @ 50% of the total project cost (Maximum amount of subsidy is ₹10,000/-).

Details
The scheme "Mahila Samrudhhi Yojana (Gujarat Gopalak Vikas Nigam)" by the Social Justice and Empowerment Department, Government of Gujarat, aims to provide Microfinance for individual women entrepreneurs to create self-employment for women and make them self-reliant. Under this scheme, loans are provided on an individual basis to women beneficiaries to start a business of their choice. The scheme is implemented by the Gujarat Gopalak Vikas Nigam.
﻿

### BENEFITS
Benefits
The scheme provides 100% of the loan amount to eligible women beneficiaries, up to a maximum limit of ₹1,25,000/-.
The loan carries an interest rate of 4% per annum.
﻿

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant should belong to the Rabari and Bharwad castes from the socially and educationally backwards classes.
The applicant should be a woman.

==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
The "Mahila Swavlamban Scheme" launched by the Women and Child Development Department, Gujarat, aims to empower women by providing financial assistance for starting or expanding economic activities. This initiative targets women from rural and urban areas, especially those from families living below the poverty line. The scheme offers a subsidy and a loan to support the economic development of women, helping them become self-reliant.
﻿
﻿

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Subsidy Support:
A subsidy of 15% or up to ₹30,000/- (whichever is lower) is provided to eligible women to support their business ventures.
Loan Facility:
Women can avail of loans up to ₹2,00,000/- to start or expand their economic activities.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant must be a woman.
The applicant must be a resident of Gujarat.
The applicant must belong to the BPL (Below Poverty Line) category
The applicant's annual income must be ₹1,20,000/- in rural areas and ₹1,50,000/-in urban areas.
﻿

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Offline
Step-1:
The applicant must fill out the prescribed form with complete details.

Submit the form along with the necessary documents to the Women's Economic Development Corporation.
Helpdesk:
Contact Details.
﻿

Documents Required
Age proof.
Aadhaar card.
Quotation for business activities.
Experience certificate.
Income proof.
Copy of Ration card.

        - Max Age: 60
        - State: Gujarat
        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/mssg
        

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the Mahila Swavlamban Scheme?
The Mahila Swavlamban Scheme is a financial assistance program aimed at empowering women from rural and urban areas to undertake economic activities.
Who is eligible for the scheme?
The applicant must be a woman with a family living below the poverty line, with an annual income of ₹1,00,000/- in rural areas and ₹1,50,000/-  in urban areas.
What financial assistance does the scheme provide?
The scheme provides a subsidy of 15% or  ₹30,000/- (whichever is lower) and loans up to Rs. 2 lakh to eligible women for business activities.
How will the loan be disbursed?
The Women's Economic Development Corporation verifies the application, approves the loan, and facilitates the disbursement through the bank.
Can women from urban areas apply for the scheme?
Yes, the scheme is open to women from both rural and urban areas who meet the eligibility criteria.
Is there any age limit for applying to the scheme?
The scheme does not specify an age limit, but the applicant must submit age proof during the application process.
What is the maximum loan amount available?
The maximum loan available under the scheme is ₹2,00,000/- for eligible women to undertake economic activities.
How is the subsidy calculated?
The subsidy is calculated at 15% of the loan amount or a maximum of ₹30,000/-, whichever is lower.
Can the loan be used for any type of business?
Yes, the loan can be used for any economic activity or business venture that supports the applicant's financial independence.
Where should the application be submitted?
The application must be submitted to the Gujarat State Women's Economic Development Corporation at their office in Gandhinagar.
What documents are required for the application?
Documents required include age proof, Aadhar card, quotation, experience certificate, income proof, and ration card copy.

SCHEME NAME: Mahila Udhyami Vishesh Protsahan Yojana
TAGS: Capital Subsidy, Entrepreneurship, Interest Subsidy, Laon, Skill Development, Woman Entrepreneur
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
﻿
The scheme "Mahila Udhyami Vishesh Protsahan Yojana" was launched by the Department of Industries, Government of Uttarakhand on 15th August 2015, with the objective of ensuring adequate participation of women in the micro and small enterprise sector, contributing to the economic development of the state. Under this scheme, a capital subsidy of up to 25% of the total fixed capital investment and an interest subsidy of 6% on bank-approved loans are provided to women entrepreneurs for setting up micro and small enterprises in the manufacturing and service sectors.
Objectives:
The main objective of the scheme is to create entrepreneurship and skill development among women and provide easy loan facility through banks for arranging the required capital for setting up enterprises, so that women can become self-reliant by setting up their own enterprises and also play the role of employment provider.
Implementation of the scheme:
The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Department will be the nodal department for the implementation of the scheme. The responsibility of implementing the scheme at the state level will be done through the Director, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Uttarakhand and at the district level through the General Manager, District Industries Centre.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
The following financial incentives will be given under the scheme:
Capital Subsidy:
25% of the total fixed capital investment, up to a maximum of ₹25,00,000/-.
Interest Subsidy:
6% of the interest payable on bank-approved loans, up to a maximum of ₹5,00,000/- per year per unit.
Conditions Associated with Benefits:
Financial incentive assistance will only be provided to enterprises that remain operational for at least 5 years after the date of receiving the subsidy; otherwise, the government reserves the right to recover the entire assistance amount.
If it is found that the unit or bank concealed facts or misrepresented them, leading to wrongful receipt of the subsidy, the disbursed subsidy amount will be recovered with interest.
Women entrepreneurs who are eligible for capital and interest subsidies under other self-employment schemes of the Central or State Government or governmental institutions have the option to apply under this scheme, choosing the one where they receive maximum benefits.
Central or State Government-operated self-employment schemes, such as the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Program, Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali Self-Employment Scheme, and Chief Minister's Self-Employment Scheme, which provide margin money or capital subsidy, will also be eligible for interest incentive benefits under this scheme as "top-up" benefits, provided there is no restriction on such facilities in those schemes.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant's new enterprise means such an enterprise that is proposed to start commercial production/activity on or after 15th August, 2015. For this purpose, the Entrepreneurs Memorandum (EM) Part-1/Entrepreneurs Memorandum (EM) Part-2 acknowledgement issued by the General Manager, District Industries Centre has been obtained.
Micro and small enterprises in the manufacturing and service sector refer to such enterprises that fall under the definition of manufacturing and service enterprises in the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act-2006 of the Government of India.
The limit of investment in plant and machinery for manufacturing enterprises is ₹25,00,000/-, ₹5,00,00,000/- and ₹10,00,00,000/-, respectively, and the limit of investment in equipment for service sector enterprises is ₹10,00,000/-, ₹2,00,00,000/- and ₹5,00,00,000/-, respectively.
An enterprise should be wholly owned by women. In case of cooperative society/committee, self-help group, partnership and private limited company, shareholding of women entrepreneur/entrepreneurs should be more than 51%.
The applicant's enterprise should be financed by a nationalized bank, a financial institution notified or authorized by the Reserve Bank of India, or a cooperative sector bank or financial institution.
﻿

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Offline
Online
To apply for the scheme, you should visit your nearest District Industries Centre with all the necessary documents and certificates.

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
A copy of the acknowledgement of the Entrepreneur Memorandum Part-1 issued by the District Industry Centre.
A copy of the acknowledgement of the Entrepreneur Memorandum Part-2 issued by the District Industry Centre.
Sanction letter of term loan/working capital sanctioned by the financing bank/financial institution for fixed assets and working capital in the approved project for the enterprise, and certificate of disbursement of the sanctioned loan.
Certified copies of bill vouchers, payment receipts/bank payment details and certificate of fixed capital investment given by authorized chartered accountant for the fixed capital investment made in the enterprise, which includes expenditure incurred in purchasing the required land, factory building, plant and machinery, fixtures, furniture, equipment etc. and installation expenses.
Statement in prescribed format, which includes installment of payment of loan taken by the new enterprise, interest imposed on the enterprise, principal and interest paid by the enterprise, rate of interest, rate of interest subsidy and calculation statement related to subsidy amount, which is certified by the branch manager or authorized officer of the concerned bank/financial institution.
Certificate from the financial institution/bank to the effect that the loan has been paid regularly in the concerned quarter and the loanee unit is not a defaulter in any way.
Any other
documents

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the main objective of the scheme?
The main objective of the scheme is to create entrepreneurship and skill development among women and provide easy loan facility through banks for arranging the required capital for setting up enterprises, so that women can become self-reliant by setting up their own enterprises and also play the role of employment provider.
What is the maximum capital subsidy an eligible enterprise can receive under this scheme?
An eligible enterprise can receive a capital subsidy of 25% of the total fixed capital investment, with a maximum limit of ₹25,00,000.
What is the annual maximum interest subsidy provided per unit under this scheme?
The scheme provides an interest subsidy of 6% on bank-approved loans, with a maximum annual limit of ₹5,00,000 per unit.
What is considered a "new enterprise" for eligibility under this scheme?
A new enterprise is one that proposes to commence commercial production or activity on or after August 15, 2015, and has obtained acknowledgement of the Entrepreneur Memorandum Part I or Part II.
What is the maximum investment limit in plant and machinery for a small manufacturing enterprise to be eligible?
For a small manufacturing enterprise, the investment in plant and machinery should not exceed ₹10,00,00,000 to be eligible under the scheme.
What is the maximum investment limit in equipment for a micro service sector enterprise?
For a micro service sector enterprise, the investment in equipment should not exceed ₹10,00,000.
Which types of financial institutions can finance an eligible enterprise under this scheme?
An eligible enterprise must be financed by a nationalised bank, a financial institution notified or authorised by the Reserve Bank of India, or a cooperative sector bank or financial institution.
Can other self-employment schemes like the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Program also receive interest incentive benefits as a "top-up" from this scheme?
Yes, schemes like PMEGP, Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali Self-Employment Scheme, and Chief Minister's Self-Employment Scheme can receive interest incentive benefits as a "top-up," provided there are no restrictions in their respective schemes.
What is the first document required to be submitted with the application for financial incentives?
A copy of the acknowledgement of Entrepreneur Memorandum Part-1 issued by the District Industry Centre is the first required document.
Besides the Entrepreneur Memorandum acknowledgements, what financial document is required from the bank?
The sanction letter of the term loan/working capital sanctioned by the financing bank/financial institution, along with the certificate of disbursement of the sanctioned loan, is required.
What kind of proof is needed for fixed capital investment made in the enterprise?
Certified copies of bill vouchers, payment receipts/bank payment details, and a certificate of fixed capital investment given by an authorised chartered accountant are required.
Who must certify the statement detailing loan payments, interest, and subsidy calculation?
The statement detailing loan payments, interest, and subsidy calculation must be certified by the branch manager or authorised officer of the concerned bank or financial institution.
What specific certificate is required from the financial institution regarding loan payment status?
A certificate from the financial institution/bank stating that the loan has been paid regularly in the concerned quarter and the loanee unit is not a defaulter in any way is required.
When can an interest subsidy claim be submitted to the District Industries Centre?
An interest subsidy claim can be submitted quarterly to the General Manager, District Industries Centre, from the first date of loan disbursement, after the unit begins commercial production and receives the Entrepreneur Memorandum Part-2 acknowledgement.
What is the maximum claim amount that can be approved by the district-level committee?
Claims up to ₹5,00,000 can be approved and paid after the approval of the district-level committee.
What is the deadline for submitting the first interest subsidy claim for a new enterprise?
The first claim for interest subsidy must be submitted within 6 months from the date the new enterprise starts commercial production or business.

SCHEME NAME: Mahtari Vandan Yojana
TAGS: Child, Financial Assistance, Mother, Widow
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
The scheme "Mahatari Vandan Yojana" by the Government of Chhattisgarh aims to provide financial assistance and support to eligible beneficiaries for socio-economic empowerment. The scheme offers monetary benefits and access to essential services, targeting underserved communities. Key eligibility criteria include residency in Chhattisgarh and possession of an EPIC Card. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Social Welfare, and applications are accepted online through the official portal.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Each eligible woman will receive ₹1000/- per month.
Women receiving less than ₹1000/- per month under social assistance programs and various pension schemes through the Samaj Kalyan Vibhag will receive additional assistance to a total ₹1,000/- per month.
The assistance will be directly deposited into the applicant's Aadhaar-linked DBT-based bank account.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant must be a resident of Chhattisgarh.
The applicant must be a married woman.
The applicant must be at least 21 years old as of 1st January of the year of application.
The applicant can also be a widow / divorced / abandoned woman.

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Offline
Step 1:
Visit the
"Mahtari Vandan Yojana" portal, c
lick on the registration link. In the
registration form,
provide required details such as name, contact information, and EPIC Card number.
Step 2:
Use the credentials you created during registration to log in. Navigate to the online form of the scheme. In the form, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload all the mandatory documents in the specified format and size. Carefully review all the information provided and the documents uploaded. Make any necessary corrections.
Step 3:
Click "Submit" to submit your application. Save the application reference number or confirmation message for future tracking.
Post-Application Processes
Step 1:
After the last date of application, a provisional list of applicants will be displayed on the portal/app. A printout of the list will also be displayed on the notice board at the Gram Panchayat/ward level.
Step 2:
The Gram Sachiv/ward in-charge will issue an approval letter to the eligible beneficiaries in the final list. This list will also be displayed on the portal.

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
Self-attested passport-size photo
Local residence document (residence certificate/ration card/voter ID card)
Aadhaar card of the applicant and her husband
PAN card of the applicant and her husband (if available)
Marriage certificate/certificate issued by the Gram Panchayat or local bodies
Husband's death certificate (in case of widow)
Certificate issued by the society/ward/Gram Panchayat (in case of abandoned woman)
Birth certificate/10th or 12th class marksheet/transfer certificate/PAN card/voter ID card/driving license (any one)
Bank account details and photocopy of the bank passbook of the eligible beneficiary
Self-declaration form/affidavit (attached with the application)
*Applicants may be required to be present at designated locations for verification of the documents submitted with their application.

### METADATA & LINKS

        - Min Age: 18
        - Max Age: 60
        - State: Chhattisgarh
        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/mvy
        

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What are the eligibility criteria regarding marital status for applying to this financial assistance scheme?
The applicant must be a married woman, widow, divorcee, or abandoned woman who is a local resident of Chhattisgarh.
Is there a minimum age requirement to qualify for the monthly financial assistance?
Yes, the applicant must be 21 years or older as of 1st January of the year of application.
How much financial assistance will an eligible woman receive under this scheme?
Each eligible beneficiary will receive ₹1,000 per month directly deposited into her Aadhaar-linked bank account.
What happens if a woman already receives some amount under other social assistance programs?
If she receives less than ₹1,000, she will get additional assistance to make the total ₹1,000 per month.
How will the financial assistance amount be disbursed to the beneficiaries?
The amount will be transferred directly into the applicant’s Aadhaar-linked DBT-enabled bank account.
Is it mandatory to have an Aadhaar-linked bank account to receive the benefits?
Yes, the applicant must have her own Aadhaar-linked DBT-based bank account to receive the assistance.
Are there any tax-related exclusions for the applicant’s family under this scheme?
Yes, no member of the applicant’s family should be an income taxpayer.
Can a woman apply if any family member is employed by the government?
No, if any family member is a government employee (permanent, temporary, or contractual), she is ineligible.
Are former or current MPs or MLAs or their family members eligible for this scheme?
No, if any family member is or was an MP, MLA, or held certain government positions, the applicant is excluded.
What documents are required to prove local residency in Chhattisgarh?
Acceptable documents include a residence certificate, ration card, or voter ID card.
Is a marriage certificate mandatory for married women applying to the scheme?
Yes, a marriage certificate or a certificate issued by the Gram Panchayat/local bodies is required.
What proof is needed if a woman is abandoned by her husband?
An abandoned woman must submit a certificate issued by the society/ward/Gram Panchayat as proof.
Which documents can be submitted as proof of age for the applicant?
Acceptable documents include a birth certificate, 10th/12th marksheet, PAN card, voter ID, or driving license.
Do applicants need to submit a self-declaration or affidavit?
Yes, a self-declaration form or affidavit must be attached with the application.

SCHEME NAME: Mai Bhago Vidya Scheme
TAGS: Education, Free Cycle, Girl Empowerment, Girl Welfare
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
Mai Bhago Vidya Scheme aims to ensure that the girl’s students continue their education beyond the level of primary, to promote girl's enrollment, and reduce the dropout of the girl child in the senior secondary and higher secondary school level.
The name Mai Bhago is one of the brave Sikh women soldiers who guided Sikh soldiers against the Mughals in 1705. She was the hero of that war because she killed a number of Mughals soldiers.
In the State, most of the girls leave their education after 8th class because schools are far away from their homes. It is not easy for them to go to school without any vehicles and most families in Punjab villages cannot afford vehicles or bicycles for their girl’s child. Mai Bhago Vidya Scheme helps those school-going girls who cannot afford the vehicles.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Free bicycles are provided to all girl students of 9th to 12th classes.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
Girl students should be residents of Punjab state.
Girl students should be studying in standards 9th,10th, 11th, and 12th in the government school.
Girl students should belong to those below the poverty line (BPL).

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Offline
Applicants can also contact the principal of their concerned school regarding the Scheme.
The application form will be provided by the concerned person.
Fill up the application form and submit all the required Documents.
Verification of the details of the applicant will be done by the concerned authority.
After successful verification, the applicant can avail the benefit of the scheme.

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
Identity card such as Aadhaar card
Resident proof
BPL card
Caste certificate if applicable
School certificate

### METADATA & LINKS

        - Max Age: 60

        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/mbvs

Mai Bhago Vidya Scheme helps those school-going girls who cannot afford vehicles.

Free bicycles are provided to all girl students.
Who can avail the benefits ?
Girl students should be in the 9th to 12th standard in the government school.
What is the financial eligibility criteria ?
Girl students should belong to those below the poverty line (BPL).
May Other State Residents Apply For The Scheme?
No, Girl students should be residents of Punjab state.
How to apply for the scheme ?
1. Applicants can also contact the principal of their concerned school regarding the Scheme. 
2. The application form will be provided by the concerned person.

SCHEME NAME: Mai Ramabai Ambedakar Saat Phera Samuh Lagna Yojana
TAGS: Financial Assistance, Group Marriage, Incentive, Scheduled Caste, Wedding
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
The scheme "Mai Ramabai Ambedakar Saat Phera Samuh Lagna Yojana" was launched by the Director of Scheduled Caste Welfare, Department of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of Gujarat, in the year 1998. Under the scheme, incentives are provided to couples who participate in group marriages, as well as to the organizing institution. If people adopt the practice of group marriages, they can avoid the unnecessary expenses associated with individual weddings and promote financial growth.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Under the scheme, couples participating in group marriages are given an incentive of ₹12,000/- per couple in the name of the bride.
For organizing Group Marriage Functions, the organizer/organizing institution will be paid an incentive of ₹3,000/- per couple up to a maximum of ₹75,000/-.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant should be a native of Gujarat.
The applicant should belong to the Scheduled Caste category.
The annual income limit in this scheme is ₹6,00,000/- in rural areas and ₹6,00,000/- in urban areas.
In case of remarriage, the benefit will not be available under this scheme.
The age limit of the girl at the time of marriage should be 18 years and the age of the boys should be 21 years. Proof of age of bride and groom to be married will be mandatory.
Applications for assistance must be made within two years of the marriage.
The beneficiary girl participating in the group marriage will be eligible for the benefits under this scheme.
The assistance of the scheme will be available to girls from Kunwar Bai Nu Mameru Yojana.
Marriage registration certificate has to be submitted compulsorily to avail the benefits of this scheme.
The organization/institution organizing the group wedding has to apply to the concerned authority within two years from the date of marriage.
The bride must produce a certified copy of the caste certificate obtained from the competent authority of the bride.

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the maintenance allowance for V.J.N.T and SBC students?
The maintenance allowance is a financial support scheme provided to V.J.N.T and SBC students pursuing professional courses and residing in hostels attached to professional colleges. It aims to assist these students with their living expenses during their education.
Who is eligible for the maintenance allowance for V.J.N.T and SBC students?
V.J.N.T and SBC students studying in professional courses, such as engineering, medicine, law, management, etc., and living in hostels attached to professional colleges are eligible for the maintenance allowance. Eligibility criteria may include proof of caste/category, income criteria, and enrollment in a recognized professional course.
How can eligible V.J.N.T and SBC students apply for the maintenance allowance?
The process for applying for the maintenance allowance may vary depending on the state or institution providing the scheme. Generally, eligible students are required to fill out an application form, provide supporting documents such as caste/category certificate, income certificate, proof of admission to a professional course, and hostel residence proof. The application is then submitted to the designated authority or institution.
What expenses are covered under the maintenance allowance for V.J.N.T and SBC students?
The maintenance allowance typically covers expenses related to food, accommodation, books, stationery, and other essential living expenses. The specific amount and coverage may vary depending on the state or institution's guidelines and the financial resources available for the scheme.
Is the maintenance allowance a scholarship or a stipend?
The maintenance allowance is usually provided as a stipend or financial support rather than a scholarship. It aims to assist V.J.N.T and SBC students with their day-to-day living expenses while pursuing their professional courses.
How often is the maintenance allowance disbursed?
The frequency of disbursement may vary depending on the state or institution's policies. In some cases, the maintenance allowance is disbursed on a monthly or quarterly basis. The specific disbursement schedule and mode of payment (such as direct bank transfer or cheque) are usually communicated to the eligible students.
Are there any conditions or obligations associated with the maintenance allowance?
The maintenance allowance may be subject to certain conditions or obligations set by the state or institution. These may include maintaining a minimum attendance or academic performance, adhering to the hostel rules and regulations, and providing periodic progress reports. It is important for students to familiarize themselves with the terms and conditions of the scheme.

SCHEME NAME: Maintenance Grant for Children with Disabilities from Birth
TAGS: BPL, Childcare, Differently Abled, Grant, PwD
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
The scheme “Maintenance Grant for Children with Disabilities from Birth” is implemented by the Department of Social Welfare, Government of Uttarakhand. It aims to provide financial assistance to parents or guardians for caring for their children below 18 years of age with more than 40% disability.
﻿

### BENEFITS
Benefits
₹700/- per month is provided to parents or guardians for caring for their children.
﻿

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
The applicant must be the parent or guardian of a child with more than 40% disability.
The child must be below 18 years of age.
The family’s monthly income must be less than ₹4,000/- or the family must belong to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.
﻿

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Online
The applicant can apply online either by themselves or through a Common Service Center (CSC) via the Department’s Pension Portal (
https://ssp.uk.gov.in
), the
UMANG
Mobile App, or the Apuni Sarkar Portal (
https://eservices.uk.gov.in
).
The following documents are mandatory at the time of applying: Applicant’s mobile number, Passport-size photograph (attested by Gram Pradhan / V.P.D.O. / certified by Councillor), Photocopy of Aadhaar card and Voter ID card, CBS bank account details (linked/seeded with Aadhaar), Valid family income certificate or BPL certificate, Certificate of disability of more than 40%, child's birth certificate, Copy of family register (for rural areas only), Copy of the resolution passed in the open meeting of Gram Panchayat (for rural areas) / certified by Councillor (for urban areas)
All the above documents must be issued from the district where the application is being submitted.
For verification of the online application form in rural areas, the final decision is taken by the District Social Welfare Officer after recommendations from the Gram Panchayat Development Officer, Assistant Social Welfare Officer, and Block Development Officer, respectively. In urban areas, verification and recommendation are done by the Assistant Social Welfare Officer and Sub-District Magistrate. If the application is found correct, the District Social Welfare Officer approves it, after which the pension payment process is initiated.
But along with the above documents, a certificate of disability of more than 40% and a UID certificate from the Chief Medical Officer will also have to be given.
The pension amount will be credited to the parent's bank account within one month after the application is approved.
﻿

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
Applicant’s mobile number
Passport-size photograph (certified by Gram Pradhan / V.P.D.O. / Councillor)
Aadhaar card
Voter ID card
CBS bank account linked/seeded with Aadhaar card
Valid family income certificate or BPL certificate
Disability certificate of child showing more than 40% disability
Child’s birth certificate
Copy of family register (for rural areas)
Copy of the resolution passed in the open meeting of the Gram Panchayat (for rural areas) or by the Councillor (for urban areas)
Note:
All the above documents must be issued from the district where the application is submitted.
﻿

### METADATA & LINKS

        - Min Age: 18
        - Max Age: 60
        - State: Uttarakhand
        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/vbpa

SCHEME NAME: Maintenance Of Pregnant Desi Indigenous Cows Ration For BPL Families
TAGS: BPL Families, Balanced Ration, Pregnant Desi Indigenous Cows
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
The Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Himachal Pradesh had introduced a scheme named "
Maintenance of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cows Ration for BPL families of all Categories of livestock farmers
" with the help of which a balanced ration of 3 kg per day for up to two cows or buffaloes for three months during the last trimester of pregnancy to BPL families shall be provided. The government and beneficiary share the cost of the ration on a 50:50 basis, and the cost of feed depends on approved rates.  This scheme may serve about 6.5 Lakh cows and buffaloes become pregnant every year in the state. This scheme may help BPL families and all categories of livestock farmers in the state to maintain a balanced and nutritious diet for pregnant Desi/Indigenous cows in the State. Maintaining a proper and balanced ration for pregnant Desi/Indigenous cows is crucial for the health of cows and the growth and development of calves. Providing a nutritious and balanced diet can also help reduce the risk of health complications during and after pregnancy.
Objectives:
Increase in milk production thereby providing more economic gains to the farmers.
To reduce the inter-calving period which will ultimately result in more calves and higher milk production.
To improve the health of pregnant cows so that their full milk production potential can be realized after parturition.
To ensure the birth of healthy calves free of diseases and malnutrition so that they grow to become higher-producing animals.
As the incentive is being given to Desi/Indigenous cows the farmers can be motivated to rear such animals.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Benefits:
The scheme for maintenance of pregnant Desi/Indigenous cows ration for BPL families of all categories of livestock farmers in Himachal Pradesh can have a significant impact on the health and livelihoods of farmers, as well as the overall development of the region. This scheme in
Himachal Pradesh can have several benefits,
such as:
Improved cow health:
A balanced and nutritious diet for pregnant cows can improve their health and reduce the risk of health complications during and after pregnancy.
Improved calf growth and development:
A well-fed pregnant cow can provide better nutrition to the growing calf, leading to better growth and development.
Increased milk production:
Adequate nutrition can improve the milk production of the cow, leading to increased income for the farmer.
Better breed quality:
The scheme can also include provisions for breed improvement, leading to better quality Desi/Indigenous cows that can provide better milk yield and meat quality.
Employment generation:
The scheme can create employment opportunities in the feed and fodder development sector, leading to better livelihoods for farmers.
Reduced poverty:
The scheme can help BPL families and all categories of livestock farmers to improve their income and reduce poverty.
Improved food security:
Improved milk production and better quality meat can contribute to better food security in the region.
Expected Outcome:
After feeding a balanced ration during the last trimester of pregnancy, milk production increased by 2 ltr/day.
With the assumption that during lactation of 300 days, the farmer will market this milk at @ 30/ltr, his income will increase by Rs.18000/year (Approx.).

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
Livestock owners belonging to BPL families of all categories rearing Desi/Indigenous/crossbred cows.
The subsidy will be provided to each BPL family of all categories maximum upto two Desi/Indigenous cows and their crosses.

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Online
Visit the official
website
of the department of the Animal Husbandry, Government of Himachal Pradesh, which implements the specific scheme.
The applicant may read the complete guidelines of the scheme for "
maintenance of pregnant Desi/Indigenous cows ration for BPL families of all categories of livestock farmers
" and if found eligible, may scroll down and click on the checkbox "
I agree with the terms & Conditions
" and click "
Proceed
" button.
Once Proceed, online
application form
open.
Fill the application form, upload the documents such as proof of BPL status, land documents, and bank account details and click Submit.
Submit the application form and documents to the concerned department or authority.
Check the status & Follow up with the concerned department to track the status of the application.
Note:
It is important for farmers to keep a copy of the application form and documents submitted for future reference. Additionally, farmers should ensure that they comply with the guidelines and regulations of the scheme to ensure that they are eligible for the benefits of the scheme.
During the application form, the applicant can enter maximum 2 in the section "
Number of Cow
" and shall be required to enter the "
Ear Tag Number
" of each cow.

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
Copy of Aadhaar card.
Copy of Bank Passbook.
Number of Cow along with their Ear Tag Number.
Copy of BPL certificate.
Copy of Pregnancy certificate.
Copy of Income certificate.
Copy of Residence proof.
Other relevant documents as listed by the department from time to time.

The scheme “
Maintenance of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme for BPL families belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC) category
” had been launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Himachal Pradesh with the aim to provides a 50% subsidy on a balanced ration for pregnant cows or buffalo during the last trimester of pregnancy. Under this scheme, balanced ration @ 3kg/day/cow or buffalo for maximum of two animals for three months during the last trimester of pregnancy at 50% subsidy of BPL families belonging to the Scheduled Caste category may be provided.
Objectives:
Increase in milk production thereby providing more economic gains to the farmers.
To reduce the inter-calving period which will ultimately result in more calves and higher milk production.
To improve the health of pregnant cows & buffaloes so that their full milk production potential can be realized after parturition.
To ensure the birth of healthy calves free of diseases and malnutrition so that they grow to become higher-producing animals.
As the incentive is being given to Desi/Indigenous cows and buffaloes, the farmers can be motivated to rear such animals.
Assumptions:
A balanced ration will be provided @ 3kg/day/cow for three months (last trimester of pregnancy).
The cost will be shared by the Government and beneficiary on a 50:50 basis.
The cost of feed will depend upon the tender/approved rates.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Ration:
3 kg of balanced ration per day for a maximum of two animals for three months.
Milk production:
Milk production increases by 2 liters per day after feeding the ration.
Income:
If the farmer sells the milk at 30 rupees per liter during the 300-day lactation period, their income may increase by approximately 18,000 rupees per year.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The beneficiary should be a permanent resident of Himachal Pradesh.
Livestock owners belonging to BPL of Scheduled Caste category families rearing Desi/Indigenous/crossbred cows or buffaloes are eligible under the scheme.
The subsidy will be provided to each BPL of Scheduled Caste category families for a maximum of up to two Desi/Indigenous cows/their crosses or buffaloes.

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Online
Visit the official
website
of the department of the Animal Husbandry, Government of Himachal Pradesh, which implements the specific scheme.
The applicant may read the complete guidelines of the scheme for "
Maintenance of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme for BPL families belonging to Scheduled Caste category
" and if found eligible, may scroll down and click on the checkbox "
I agree with the terms & Conditions
" and click "
Proceed
" button.
Once Proceed, online
application form
open.
Fill the application form, upload the documents such as proof of BPL status, land documents, and bank account details and click Submit.
Submit the application form and documents to the concerned department or authority.
Check the status & Follow up with the concerned department to track the status of the application.
Note:
It is important for farmers to keep a copy of the application form and documents submitted for future reference. Additionally, farmers should ensure that they comply with the guidelines and regulations of the scheme to ensure that they are eligible for the benefits of the scheme.
During the application form, the applicant can enter maximum 2 in the section "

" and shall be required to enter the "

" and "

" of each cow.

SCHEME NAME: Makhana Beej Vitaran
TAGS: Agriculture, Financial Assistance, Makhana Seed Distribution, Seed Supply, Subsidy
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
“Makhana Beej Vitaran” launched by the Department of Agriculture, Bihar, aims to enhance Makhana cultivation and increase farmers' earnings. Under this scheme, improved seed varieties such as Swarn Vaidehi and Sabour Makhana-1, developed by Bihar Agricultural University, are distributed to farmers in 11 districts of Bihar.
The scheme is to be implemented in 10 districts of the state under Schedule 1, 2 and 3 of the approval order, namely, Katihar, Purnia, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Kishanganj, Supaul, Araria, Madhepura, Saharsa and Khagaria.
﻿

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Subsidized Seeds:
Seeds of recommended varieties will be made available to farmers at the rate of 30 Kg/Ha.
For Swarn Vaidehi variety:
₹4,950/- will be given as a subsidy (75%).
For Sabour Makhana-1 variety:
₹5,737.50/- will be given as a subsidy (75%).
﻿

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant should be a farmer.
The applicant should belong to any of the following districts of Bihar: Katihar, Purnia, Madhubani, Kishanganj, Supaul, Araria, Madhepura, Saharsa, Darbhanga, Sitamarhi and Khagaria.
The applicant must have agricultural land a minimum of 0.25 acres (0.1 ha) and a maximum of 10 acres (4 ha).
The applicant must be registered on the DBT portal.
﻿
Note 1
:  Beneficiary allocation:
Women Participation: 30%.
Note 2:
The benefits of this scheme can be taken by ryot farmers on the basis of land documents and non-ryot farmers on the basis of contract form.
Note 3:
Beneficiaries will be selected on first come first serve basis.

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Online
DBT Registration Process:
Step 1:
Visit the
registration page
of the DBT portal.
Step 2:
Select Aadhaar verification type: OTP/ BIO-AUTH/ IRIS.
Step 3:
Enter your Aadhaar number and Name as per Aadhaar. Click on “Authentication”.
Step 4:
Enter the OTP. Click on “Validate OTP”.
Step 5:
Now confirm the details about the “Kisan Credit Card (KCC)” Details. Click on “Farmer Registration”.
Step 6:
In the Registration Page, fill in all the details properly i.e. Farmer details, Land information, Bank account details and click on “Submit”.
Step 7:
Validate with OTP. Click on “Register” to generate the Registration Id.
Note:
After 48 hours of registration, farmers can apply for the scheme with the help of 13 digit registration number.
﻿
Online Application of the Scheme:
Step 1:
Visit the official
website
.
Step 2:
Scroll to bottom and confirm the checkbox. Click on “Proceed to apply”.
Step 3:
In the next page select the “Type of Applicant” and enter the “DBT Registration Number of Kisan”. Click on “Get details”.
Step 4:
Fill in the required details i.e. Address, Land Details, etc, and upload documents.
Step 5:
Confirm the checkbox and then click on “Submit”.
Step 6:
An “Application Number” will be generated. Keep this for future reference.
Step 7:
Printout of the filled in application also can be taken using the Print option.

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
For DBT Registration Process:
Aadhaar Details (Should be linked with mobile number).
Passport Size Photo.
Farmer details.
Land information.
Bank account.
For the Online Application of the Scheme:
Passport Size Photo.
﻿
Contract form
( for non-ryot farmers).
Land-ownership/ revenue receipt (If applicable).
Note:
If the applicant's name is not clear in the land-ownership/ revenue receipt, it will be mandatory to attach the genealogy along with the land-ownership/ revenue receipt.

### METADATA & LINKS

        - Min Age: 18
        - Max Age: 60
        - State: Bihar
        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/mbyb
        

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the purpose of the “Makhana Beej Vitaran” Scheme?
The scheme aims to increase farmers' income by improving the production and productivity of Makhana through the distribution of high-quality seeds.
Which districts are eligible for the scheme?
Farmers from Katihar, Purnia, Madhubani, Kishanganj, Supaul, Araria, Madhepura, Saharsa, Darbhanga, Sitamarhi, and Khagaria are eligible for the scheme.
Who can avail benefits from this scheme?
Farmers who own or lease land in the eligible districts can avail benefits from the scheme.
What types of seeds are distributed under the scheme?
The scheme provides improved varieties of Makhana seeds, including Swarna Vaidehi and Sabour Makhana-1.
What is the subsidy offered under this scheme?
A 75% subsidy is provided on the total cost of seeds per hectare for both Swarna Vaidehi and Sabour Makhana-1 varieties.
What is the cost of Swarna Vaidehi seeds after subsidy?
For Swarna Vaidehi seeds, the total cost per hectare is ₹6,600/-, and the subsidy of ₹4,950/- makes it highly affordable for farmers.
What is the cost of Sabour Makhana-1 seeds after subsidy?
For Sabour Makhana-1 seeds, the total cost per hectare is ₹7,650/-, and the subsidy of ₹5,737.50/- significantly reduces the expense for farmers.
Can tenant farmers apply for the scheme?
Yes, tenant farmers can apply by submitting an agreement in the prescribed format available through the scheme.
What is the minimum and maximum land area eligible for assistance?
Assistance is available for a minimum of 0.25 acres (0.1 hectare) and a maximum of 10 acres (4 hectares).
Where are the seeds sourced from?
The seeds are provided by Bihar Agricultural University, Sabour, Bhagalpur.

### DESCRIPTION
Details
“Makhana Vikas Yojona” launched by the Department of Agriculture, Bihar, is designed to boost the cultivation and productivity of Makhana in 10 designated districts of Bihar. The scheme is to be implemented in 10 districts of the state under Schedule 1, 2 and 3 of the approval order, namely, Katihar, Purnia, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Kishanganj, Supaul, Araria, Madhepura, Saharsa and Khagaria.

Training:

Equipment Kits:

### ELIGIBILITY

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the purpose of “Makhana Vikas Yojona”?
The purpose of “Makhana Vikas Yojona” is to promote Makhana cultivation, enhance productivity, provide improved seeds, and support farmers with financial assistance and modern agricultural practices.
Which districts are eligible under the scheme?
The scheme is implemented in 10 districts of Bihar: Katihar, Purnia, Madhubani, Kishanganj, Supaul, Araria, Madhepura, Saharsa, Darbhanga, and Khagaria.
What is the minimum and maximum land area required to apply for the scheme?
Farmers with a minimum of 0.25 acres (0.1 hectare) and a maximum of 10 acres (4 hectares) are eligible to apply for the scheme.
Can Non-Rayat farmers apply for the scheme?
Yes, Non-Rayat farmers can apply for the scheme based on a formal agreement, the format of which is available for download online.
What financial assistance is provided for purchasing traditional tools?
Farmers are eligible for a grant covering 75% of the cost of traditional tools used in Makhana cultivation, up to ₹16,575/- per kit.
What documents are required for farmers to apply for the scheme?
Farmers need to provide documents such as a land ownership certificate, updated revenue receipt, or a valid agreement in the case of Non-Rayat farmers.
How is financial assistance disbursed to farmers?
Financial assistance is disbursed directly to the bank accounts of farmers through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system.
Is training provided to farmers under the scheme?
Yes, the scheme includes training programs to educate farmers on modern techniques for Makhana cultivation and productivity improvement.
What percentage of beneficiaries under the scheme are reserved for women?
The scheme ensures that at least 30% of the selected beneficiaries each year are women.
What is the source of the seeds distributed under the scheme?
The seeds are sourced from research institutions such as the National Research Center for Makhana in Darbhanga and Bhola Paswan Shastri Agricultural College in Purnia.
Are farmers allowed to procure seeds independently?
Under certain components of the scheme, farmers can procure seeds from their own sources if they meet the specified criteria.
What types of equipment are eligible for grants under the scheme?
Traditional tools such as Aunka/Ganj, Kara, Khainchi, Chalni, Chatai, Afra, and Thaapi, used in various stages of Makhana cultivation and processing, are eligible for grants.

SCHEME NAME: Male Pig Distribution Scheme
TAGS: Animal, Male Pig, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
The "Male Pig Distribution Scheme", implemented by the Animal Husbandry Department, Government of Chhattisgarh, provides financial assistance to beneficiaries from the Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) categories for purchasing one male pig of an improved breed (Middle White Yorkshire).
The beneficiary can purchase one breeding male pig of Middle White Yorkshire breed, aged 6 months to 1 year, from a government pig rearing project or locally.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
90% of the unit cost (purchase price) or a maximum subsidy of ₹3,500/-, whichever is lower (for Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST)  category).

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant should belong to the Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe category.
The applicant should be a resident of Chhattisgarh.
The beneficiary should purchase a male pig of the improved breed (Middle White Yorkshire).
The pig should be between the 6th months the 1st year of age.
The purchase should be made from a Government-rearing project or a local authorized source.

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Offline
Step 1:
The eligible beneficiary should fill out the prescribed application form, including mandatory details like bank account information, and submit it to the Gram Panchayat for recommendation.
Step 2:
The recommended application should be sent to the Janpad Panchayat for approval and then forwarded to the District Panchayat (Agriculture Standing Committee) for final approval.
Step 3:
After approval, the District Officer should direct the selected beneficiary to purchase the breeding male pig from a government pig rearing center or locally.
Step 4:
The purchase should be physically verified by the Sarpanch, Urban Councillor, local Veterinary Assistant Surgeon, and Assistant Veterinary Field Officer. The verified bill and Panchayat fee receipt (if applicable) should be submitted to the District Officer.
Step 5:
Upon successful verification, the District Officer should transfer the prescribed grant amount to the beneficiary’s bank account and notify the beneficiary.

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
ID proof
Bank Account Details.
Caste Certificate
Any Other documents (if required).
﻿

### METADATA & LINKS

        - Min Age: 18
        - Max Age: 60
        - State: Chhattisgarh
        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/mpds
        

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the Male Pig Distribution Scheme?
The scheme provides financial assistance to SC/ST beneficiaries in Chhattisgarh for purchasing a male pig of an improved breed (Middle White Yorkshire).
Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
The applicant should belong to the Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) category and be a resident of Chhattisgarh.
What financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
Beneficiaries receive a subsidy of 90% of the unit cost or a maximum of ₹3,500, whichever is lower.
What type of pig can be purchased under the scheme?
The beneficiary can purchase a breeding male pig of the Middle White Yorkshire breed, aged between 6 months and 1 year.
Where can the pig be purchased from?
The pig should be purchased from a government pig rearing project or a locally authorized source.
What is the age requirement for the pig to be purchased?
The pig should be between 6 months to 1 year old at the time of purchase.
How is the application approved?
After recommendation by the Gram Panchayat, the application is sent to the Janpad Panchayat and then to the District Panchayat (Agriculture Standing Committee) for final approval.
How will the beneficiary receive the subsidy?
After verification, the subsidy amount will be directly transferred to the beneficiary’s bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
Who verifies the purchase of the pig?
The purchase is verified by the Sarpanch, Urban Councillor, local Veterinary Assistant Surgeon, and Assistant Veterinary Field Officer.
Is there a deadline to apply for the scheme?
There may be specific timelines for applications, depending on government notifications. It is best to check with the Animal Husbandry Department for the latest updates.

SCHEME NAME: Mamata Scheme
TAGS: Financial Assistance, Maternity Benefit, Nutritional Support, Pregnant Women And New Mothers
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
In order to improve the process in curbing the high rate of mortality and infant mortality rate, the Department of Women and Child Development, Government of Odisha introduced a scheme named "
MAMATA
" - a conditional cash transfer maternity benefit scheme in 2011.
Aim of the scheme:
Contribute in reducing the maternal and infant mortality.
Improve the health and nutrition status of pregnant and lactating mother and their infants.
Objectives of the scheme:
To provide partial wage loss compensation for the pregnant and nursing mothers with the aim to provide complete rest before and after the child birth.
Increase in utilization of child health services especially immunization.
Improve mother and child care practices.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Rs.3,000 shall be given during the third trimester of the pregnancy of the mother till delivery on completing the following 5 conditions:
Pregnancy registered at AWC/Mini AWC
Received at least 2 antenatal checkup (ANC)
Received IFA and calcium tablets.
Received at least 1 TT vaccination (out of optimal 2)
Received at least 1 counselling session at AWC/Village Health/ Home Visit.
The first 4 conditions shall be verified from MCP Card. On completing the above requirements first instalment shall be released.
Rs.2,000 shall be after completion of 10 months after delivery on fulfilment of following conditions:
Child birth is registered at AWC or HSC.
Child has received BCG vaccination.
Child has received Pentavalent 1 & 2 & 3 vaccinations.
Child has received Polio 1 & 2 & 3 vaccinations.
Child has received Rotavirus 1 & 2 & 3 vaccinations.
Child has received Measles vaccine before attaining 1 year of age.
Child has received Vitamin-A first dose before attaining 1 year of age
Mother has attended at least six Growth Monitoring and IYCF counselling sessions after delivery till 9 months
Child has been exclusively breastfed for first six months (self-certification by the beneficiary)
Child has been introduced to complementary food on completion of six months of age (self- certification by the beneficiary)
Child is being fed age-appropriate complementary feeding and continuing (self- certification by the beneficiary)
Note:
Overall, Rs.5,000 in two instalments as incentive is provided to mothers.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant must be a resident of Odisha.
The scheme is primarily aimed at pregnant women.
Pregnant & Lactating women of 19 years of age and above for the first two live births, except all Government/Public Sector Undertakings (Central and State) employees and their wives will be covered.

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Online
Offline
MAMATA mobile Application may be downloaded using URL: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.emamata.odisha&hl=en_IN&pli=1
The beneficiary may also log in on the department portal to apply for the scheme. URL: https://emamata.odisha.gov.in/login
In case the beneficiary has forgotten the password, the same can be reset by visiting URL : https://emamata.odisha.gov.in/public/forgot/password

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
Proof of Identity (any 1 of the following):
Aadhar Card
Voter ID
Passport
PAN Card
Proof of Residence (any 1 of the following):
Ration Card
Utility Bill (Electricity, Water, Gas)
Rent Agreement or Property Tax Receipt
Proof of Pregnancy:
Medical Certificate or Pregnancy Record from a government health center or Anganwadi center
Income Certificate:
Certificate issued by a government authority proving your family's income (if income criteria apply)
Bank Account Details:
Bank passbook or a recent bank statement for the account where the financial assistance will be credited
Aadhaar Enrollment Slip or Acknowledgement (if Aadhaar card is not yet received)
Photographs:
Recent passport-sized photographs of the applicant
Maternity Record:
Maternity registration record or any relevant documents from health services.
Previous Beneficiary Status (if applicable):
Any documentation if you have received benefits from similar schemes previously.
﻿

SCHEME NAME: Mamta Taruni Abhiyan
TAGS: Abhiyan, Healthcare, Mamta, Taruni
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
Details
Under this program, free medical check-ups, iron and folic acid supplements, and deworming medication were provided to adolescent girls between the ages of 10 and 19 years, and pregnant women. The program also aimed to create awareness about menstrual hygiene, family planning, and nutrition among adolescent girls and pregnant women.
The program was implemented through a network of health workers, including Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs), and Anganwadi workers. The Mamta Taruni Abhiyan was seen as a significant step towards improving maternal and child health in rural areas of Gujarat.
﻿

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Benefits
Access to Health and Wellness Services: The scheme provides access to various health and wellness services, including health check-ups, antenatal care, postnatal care, and nutritional support.
Improved Maternal and Child Health: The scheme aims to improve maternal and child health outcomes by providing timely and quality healthcare services to pregnant women and young girls.
Health Education: The scheme also provides health education and awareness sessions to beneficiaries, which helps them make informed decisions about their health and well-being.
Empowerment of Women and Girls: The scheme aims to empower women and girls by providing them with knowledge and skills related to health and nutrition, which helps them lead healthy and productive life.
Financial Support: The scheme also provides financial support to pregnant women in the form of a cash incentive, which helps them meet their medical and nutritional needs.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
Eligibility
Adolescent Girls: The scheme is open to all adolescent girls between the ages of 10 and 19 years who are residents of Gujarat.
Pregnant Women: The scheme is open to all pregnant women who are residents of Gujarat.
BPL Families: The scheme gives priority to women and girls belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Offline
Application Process
Visit the Nearest Health Center: The first step is to visit the nearest healthcare center or hospital that is authorized to provide the benefits and services under the scheme.
Fill the Application Form: The healthcare center will provide an application form for the scheme. The applicant needs to fill the form accurately and completely.
Submit Required Documents: Along with the application form, the applicant needs to submit the required documents such as identification proof, address proof, medical certificate (in case of pregnant women), and income certificate (in case of BPL families).
Get Enrolled: After submitting the application form and the required documents, the healthcare center will verify the information provided by the applicant. If the applicant is found to be eligible, they will be enrolled in the scheme.
Receive Benefits and Services: Once enrolled, the beneficiary can avail the benefits and services under the scheme, which may include health check-ups, antenatal care, postnatal care, nutritional support, health education, and financial support (in case of pregnant women).

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
List of required documents
Identification Documents: Beneficiaries must have identification documents such as a birth certificate, Aadhaar card, or any other valid government-issued identity proof.
Medical Certificate: Pregnant women may be required to provide a valid medical certificate indicating their pregnancy status and health condition.
Bank Account Details: Beneficiaries may need to provide their bank account details to receive financial support under the scheme.
Income Certificate: Women and girls belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families may need to provide an income certificate as proof of their eligibility.
Address Proof: Beneficiaries may need to provide an address proof such as a utility bill or a rent agreement to establish their residence in Gujarat.

### METADATA & LINKS

        - Min Age: 18
        - Max Age: 60
        - State: Gujarat
        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/mta

The scheme is open to adolescent girls and pregnant women who are residents of Gujarat. Women and girls belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families are given priority.

The scheme provides access to health and wellness services such as health check-ups, antenatal care, postnatal care, and nutritional support. It also provides health education and awareness sessions to beneficiaries and financial support to pregnant women in the form of a cash incentive

Pregnant women are provided a cash incentive of Rs. 6000 under the scheme to meet their medical and nutritional needs.

The differently abled person should be declared unsuitable for physical work by the respective Medical officer.

        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/mgy
        

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What does the scheme aim to provide?
The scheme offers financial assistance and employment/tool kits to Scheduled Caste individuals who aspire to establish cottage industries for self-employment, without relying on bank loans.
What are the benefits offered under the scheme?
Tool kits are provided for 28 types of trades/businesses, including handicraft work, tailoring, vehicle servicing, and carpentry, among others.
Who is eligible to apply for the scheme?
Applicants must belong to the Scheduled Caste category, be natives of Gujarat, and aged between 18 to 60 years.
Is there an income limit for applicants?
Yes, applicants from the Scheduled Caste category must have an annual family income of up to ₹6,00,000/-. However, there is no income limit for applicants belonging to the Most Backward Caste among the Scheduled Castes.
Can previous beneficiaries or their family members reapply for the scheme?
No, if the beneficiary or any family members have already availed benefits under the scheme, they are not eligible for reapplication.
Where can eligible applicants apply for the scheme?
Eligible applicants can apply through the e-Samaj Kalyan Portal: https://esamajkalyan.gujarat.gov.in/
How many types of trades/businesses are covered under the scheme?
A total of 28 types of trades/businesses are covered under the scheme, ranging from handicraft work to mobile repairing.
Can applicants from outside Gujarat apply for the scheme?
No, only native residents of Gujarat are eligible to apply for the "Manav Garima Yojana" scheme.
What is the significance of providing employment/tool kits?
Providing employment/tool kits ensures that individuals have the necessary resources to start their businesses, reducing dependency on external sources like bank loans.



==================================================
SCHEME NAME: Manav Kalyan Yojana
TAGS: Artisan, Employment, Toolkit, Trade, Voucher
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
Launched on 11th September 1995, the scheme "Manav Kalyan Yojana" implemented by the Commissioner of Cottage and Rural Industries, Industries & Mines Department, Government of Gujarat, aims to uplift economically disadvantaged sections by providing toolkit assistance (via e-vouchers) for self-employment in 10 designated trades. The scheme replaces previous self-employment initiatives and targets individuals/families with an annual income of up to ₹6,00,000/- in rural/urban areas. It focuses on empowering artisans and marginalized communities, including SC/ST and nomadic tribes, with no income limit for the most backward sub-castes. Applications are submitted online via the e-Kutir portal, and beneficiaries receive toolkits through a transparent e-voucher system.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Toolkit Assistance:
E-vouchers for toolkits in 10 specified trades.
Trades Covered:
Dairy Product Sales, Plumber, Bharat Kaam (Embroidery), Centering Work, Beauty Parlor, Electric Appliances Repairing, Papad Making, Pickle Making, Vehicle Servicing, Puncture Kit
*The maximum cost limits per toolkit are predefined (exact amounts not specified in the document).
Training Option:
Applicants can opt for skill training during the application process.
Transparent Disbursement:
E-vouchers (QR codes) are generated post-approval and redeemed at approved dealers.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicants must be between 18 and 60 years of age to qualify for the scheme.
The applicants from Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), or Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC) nomadic tribes are eligible without any income proof requirement.
The applicants from general categories must have a family annual income of ₹6,00,000/- or less, and must submit an income certificate as proof.
﻿
Additional Requirement for Rural Applicants
The rural applicants must -
a) either be listed in the Below Poverty Line (BPL) list with a poverty score of 0 to 16.
b) or submit an income certificate issued by the relevant authority.
﻿
Income Criteria Exemptions
The income limit does not apply to the following:
a) Individuals from the 12 most backward sub-castes within the Scheduled Castes.
b) Members of the most backward, nomadic, or de-notified tribes under the SEBC category.
*For all other applicants, the annual family income must not exceed ₹6,00,000/-, whether residing in rural or urban areas.

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
Who can apply for the toolkit assistance under this scheme?
Individuals aged 18-60 years from economically weaker sections (annual income ≤ ₹6,00,000/-) can apply, with no income limit for SC/ST/SEBC nomadic tribes and 12 most backward SC sub-castes.
What types of toolkits are available under this scheme?
The scheme covers 10 trades including dairy product sales, plumbing, beauty parlors, electric appliance repair, and papad/pickle making, with predefined maximum cost limits for each toolkit.
How do I prove my eligibility if I belong to the general category?
General category applicants must submit an income certificate (issued by Taluka Mamlatdar/Municipal Officer) showing family income ≤ ₹6,00,000/- annually. Rural applicants additionally need BPL listing (score 0–16) or an income certificate.
Is there any income proof requirement for SC/ST/SEBC applicants?
No, applicants from SC/ST/SEBC nomadic tribes and the 12 most backward SC sub-castes are exempt from income criteria. Only a valid caste certificate is required.
How will I receive the toolkit if my application is approved?
Approved beneficiaries receive an e-voucher (QR code) via SMS, which can be redeemed at approved dealers in Gujarat for toolkits within the scheme’s price limits.
Can I purchase tools beyond the scheme’s price limit?
Yes, but you must pay the extra amount yourself. The e-voucher covers only up to the predefined maximum cost for your selected toolkit.
Is training provided under this scheme?
Yes, applicants can opt for skill training during the application process, though details of training duration/location are not specified in the document.
What happens if I misuse the toolkit or don’t use it for its intended purpose?
Post-purchase physical verification is conducted by officials. Misuse/non-usage may lead to subsidy recovery and penal action.
Can I correct mistakes after submitting my registration details?
Yes, a confirmation pop-up appears before final submission. Click "Cancel" to edit incorrect details, then re-register.
How can I track or modify my submitted application?
Click "View Application" on the portal. Use "Print Application" for hard copies or "Modify" (if application is returned for revisions).

The Department of Social Justice would prepare a list of dental colleges and dental treatment centers from where the beneficiaries could avail treatment. It would also ensure the quality of artificial teeth and quality treatment by setting standards and norms.

### BENEFITS

The applicants should be from Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.
The persons who have completely lost their teeth or those who have partially lost their teeth and are in a position to have them extracted as they are unusable are eligible to apply under the scheme.
The persons who have been certified by a qualified dentist in the prescribed form as unfit for placing artificial teeth.
Note:
The priority will be given to the oldest person under the scheme.

SCHEME NAME: Mangalya Scheme For Widow Remarriage
TAGS: Divorced Woman, Financial Assistance, Remarriage, Widow, Woman
==================================================

### DESCRIPTION
Details
The “Mangalya Scheme” was launched by the Department of Women and Child Development, Government of Kerala. Under the scheme, financial assistance is to be provided to eligible widows and divorced women for their remarriage. In Kerala, women not only outnumber men but also outlive them, so the marital status of women in Kerala is very important. It could influence the overall care and support they receive from their family and society. Statics show only 3.5% of the total male population in Kerala are widowers and the proportion of the widowed female population is 11.56%. This gender gap adversely affects women in every sphere of their life. It is in this context, that the Government of Kerala envisages the scheme called ‘Mangalya’ to encourage widow remarriage. The scheme imparts financial assistance for the widows/divorced to remarry.

### BENEFITS
Benefits
Under the scheme, financial assistance of ₹25000/- is provided to eligible widows and divorced women to remarry.

### ELIGIBILITY
Eligibility
The applicant should be a resident of Kerala State.
The applicant should be a widow and a divorced woman.
Women belonging to the age group of 18 to 50 years who are legally divorced and widowed are eligible to apply under the scheme.

### HOW TO APPLY
Application Process
Offline
To avail of the scheme's benefits, the application duly filled out should be forwarded to District Women and Child Officers through Child Development Project Officers.

### DOCUMENTS REQUIRED
Documents Required
The following particulars should be attached to the application form:
1.	Identity proof
2.	Proof of remarriage/remarriage certificate
3.	Death Certificate of the first Husband
4.	Legal document of divorce (For divorced women)
5.	Proof of BPL/Priority Category
6.	Proof of age in the form of a school leaving certificate or certificate issued by the competent authority
7.	Certificate from Village officer showing that husband has deserted the woman for over 7 years (for such applicant)
8.	Copy of bank passbook

### METADATA & LINKS

        - Min Age: 18
        - Max Age: 60
        - State: Kerala
        - Link: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/mswr
        

### FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the “Mangalya Scheme”?
Under the scheme, financial assistance is to be provided to eligible widows and divorced women for their remarriage.
Which department has launched this scheme?
Department of Women and Child Development, Government of Kerala
What is the benefit of the scheme?
Under the scheme, financial assistance of ₹25000/- is provided to eligible widows and divorced women to remarry.
Who is eligible to get the benefits under the scheme?
Women who are legally divorced and widowed are eligible to apply under the scheme.
Is this scheme only for a resident of Kerala?
Yes, the applicant should be a resident of Kerala State.
What is the age limit to apply under the scheme?
Women belonging to the age group of 18 to 50 years are eligible to apply under the scheme.

To avail of the scheme's benefits, the application duly filled out should be forwarded to District Women and Child Officers through Child Development Project Officers.
